title: Piece values: counting what you win and lose (part 4 of 4)
outcomes: Says the counting value of each piece and which of two pieces is worth more

steps.prompt: A rook for a bishop and a pawn: how many points does it cost you, and how many do you get? Write the net result.

steps.prompt: Teach it. Explain to a friend why a queen for two minor pieces loses points even though you end up with more pieces.

fields.label: Your explanation in your own words

steps.text: **Compare with your own words.** Values: pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9. To judge a capture I count attackers and defenders, send the cheapest piece first, add what I take, subtract what I lose, and stop if it stops paying. It is a rule of thumb: checkmate and a piece that cannot move can beat the count.
